newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares edge up, sentiment still weak.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares edge up, sentiment still weak.

text.p: Shanghai B shares edged up at midday on Friday on a technical rebound after Thursday's sharp falls, but market sentiment is still weak with investor confidence seriously hurt, brokers said.
The B index inched up 0.034 points or 0.04 percent to 75.810 points on thin volume of 4.197 million shares worth $2.825 million.
Brokers said the market rallied in the early part of the morning session and then fell, indicating the short-term trend is not optimistic.
The market saw a technical rebound after the recent sharp losses, but investors are uncertain about where the bottom is, making them cautious about trading, they said.

"The market digested all the positive market factors before July 1, and now the index is in the process of digesting negative factors such as poor results for most listed firms and more strict supervision from the government," one broker said.

"The morning's gains were a technical rebound," another broker said. "Most shares were oversold over the past two days. But technical charts show a downward trend and people expect a bear run in the absense of positive factors."
Of 45 B shares, 28 traded, with 14 up, four flat and 10 down.
Shanghai Sanmao Textiles was the star on bargain-hunting, up $0.008 or 5.71 percent to $0.148 on volume of 45,000 shares.
Hainan Airlines was the most actively traded on domestic buying, gaining $0.016 or 3.07 percent to $0.536 on volume of 978,000 shares.
Shanghai's A index was weaker on poor market sentiment, and most institutions were seen continuing to liquidate their positions despite over-sold signs, brokers said.
The index fell 6.955 points or 0.58 percent to 1,195.328 points on volume of 217.9 million shares worth 2.5 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index dipped 16.866 points or 0.44 percent to 3,780.092 points.
Shanghai First Provision Store was the biggest loser on expectations of poor interim results, slipping 0.56 yuan or 6.47 percent to 8.09 yuan on volume of 243,600 shares.
